Subject: Singapore dedicated pool request - production by July

Hi Stephanie,

Following our pilot, we'd like to move Neptune Health to a dedicated APAC pool for production. Target go-live: first week of July (user-facing API). Traffic profile: 200–300 concurrent sessions at peak, average request length 350 tokens, occasional long-context batches (~3–4% of traffic).

Key asks:
- Dedicated pool physically in SG region (data residency)
- SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime, p95 latency < 250ms
- Clear lead time for procurement & invoice cycles (we're on a June board approval timeline)

Can Redwood provide a sizing recommendation and an initial SOW/estimate? Happy to schedule a short kickoff this week.

Thanks,
Danielle
Head of Platform, Neptune Health

Subject: Re: Singapore dedicated pool request - production by July

Quick sizing note based on the profile Danielle provided (200–300 concurrent, avg 350 tokens):
- Baseline recommended: 4 x A10G GPUs (mixed workload) for steady-state + 2 x A100 (burst for long-context inference) to meet p95 <250ms at peak with room for maintenance windows.
- Alternate conservative config: 6 x A10G (no A100) if customer prefers homogeneous hardware — higher queueing risk during long-context spikes.
- KV cache + prefix caching expected to reduce effective token compute by ~18% given Neptune's repeated patient prompt patterns (we'll tune cache policies during onboarding).

Estimated token capacity/second (approx):
- 4xA10G + 2xA100: ~18k tokens/sec sustained
- 6xA10G: ~14k tokens/sec sustained

I've attached a quick capacity calc (neptune_capacity_calc_v1.xlsx) with assumptions. Notes: quantization to int8 on A10G yields cost savings but we should validate accuracy on the prompt set. Also recommend canary rollout traffic split (10% -> 40% -> 100%) over 2 weeks.

If this looks reasonable, I'll turn this into a final capacity page for the SOW.

-Markus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
